header.name: Cellular biophysics
header.description: This course is designed to develop a fundamental and advanced knowledge of cellular biophysics and physiology. These are prerequisites so that students can grasp the major mechanisms underlying the functioning of a living cell. It will introduce students to the physical and mathematical toolbox to understand the various pathways that control signal transduction and intracellular signalling pathways, crucial for cell viability and functioning. This will include the study of structure-function relationships involving receptor-mediated channels, ion channels, etc., in membranes. Moreover, students will be acquainted with a few crucial methods that are extensively employed for real-time exploration and visualisation of such biophysical processes.
prerequisites_desirable: Foundations of Biology (BIO101) or equivalent for PG
prerequisites_desirable_resolved: Foundations of Biology (BIO101) or equivalent for PG

outcomes.label: CO1
outcomes.raw_text: Students will build knowledge on the fundamental architecture and physical principles underlying the functioning of a living cell

outcomes.label: CO2
outcomes.raw_text: Students will develop quantitative interpretations of various solute and nutrient transport across membranes to support cellular homeostasis.

outcomes.label: CO3
outcomes.raw_text: Students will apply the biophysical principles of the cellular mechanisms of sending messages and correlate their modulation in pathological conditions.

outcomes.label: CO4
outcomes.raw_text: Students can explain the outline of a few crucial computational and physical methods that are utilized to study cellular biophysics.

lecture_topics: Overview of the structure and physical properties of cell membrane
composition and dynamics of cell membrane
origin of surface charge, diffusion and transport across membranes
Quantitative description of surface charge and diffusion through membranes
Electrical double layer model, electrochemical potential, etc., with relevance to cells
Simple diffusion (Fick's law), Osmosis and osmotic pressure (van’t Hoff Laws)
Simple and facilitated transport across membranes
Ion permeation and membrane potential (Nernst potential, Donnan potential)
Channel and carrier-mediated transport (Na+-K+ transport, glucose transport, etc)

weekly_plan.tutorial_assignment: Quiz 2 and Assignment 2 (Assignment 2 will be on the simulation of transport across biological membrane)

lecture_topics: G-protein coupled receptors and second messengers
Computational methods (e.g., density functional theory) and experimental methods (e.g., optical microscopy, flow cytometry, etc.) for studying cellular biophysics
